stories.title: 17 dead and dozens injured in Kyiv after Russian strikes
stories.summary: Russian strikes on Ukraine's capital killed at least 17 people and wounded dozens, after the country's air force warned of incoming ballistic missiles, according to local authorities. Explosions were heard in the city shortly after midnight local time. Kyiv's military administration said the missile and drone barrage damaged residential buildings and several warehouses. "Ballistic interceptors are what could have saved the lives of those killed today," Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky said, announcing 17 people had been killed. Ukraine shot down 98 of the 115 drones fired by Russia overnight, the air force said. But it was unable to shoot down any of the missiles, preliminary statistics from the air force showed.

stories.title: Donald Trump set to travel to Doonbeg for Irish Open
stories.summary: US President Donald Trump is set to travel to Ireland next month for a visit that will include his attendance at the Irish Open at his golf course in Doonbeg, Co Clare, and events in Dublin. This date is to ensure he will be in the US for the annual commemoration of the 11 September terrorist attacks, and that he will be in Doonbeg in time for the end of the Irish Open on 13 September. Mr Trump's visit will also include a trip to Dublin, which is likely to involve a meeting with Taoiseach Micheál Martin. However, sources said it is highly unlikely that Mr Trump will give a speech to the Dáil or Seanad, or attend any events at Leinster House, as TDs and senators are not due to return from their summer break until 16 September.

stories.title: A new state investment scheme is coming. Will it work for you?
stories.summary: Analysis: The Minister for Finance is right that savers are getting 'screwed over', but it remains to be seen if the new initiative fixes this Irish households had €175 billion sitting in the bank at the end of May, earning an average of about 0.25%*, while prices rose 3.4% in the year to June. Prices are rising faster than the interest, so savings buy less each year. On Budget Day, 6 October, Minister for Finance Simon Harris will announce a new savings and investment account. The first accounts should open in 2027, and your money would go into funds that buy shares on the stock market. That is a different thing from money in the bank. Harris says savers are getting "screwed over", and that this is not for the wealthy who are doing fine, but for the garda married to the nurse. He is right about the problem. Whether this fixes it is a different question, and one already tested elsewhere. Investing in Ireland is taxed heavily and the rules are awkward. You pay 33% on money you make from shares and 38% on many funds. There is also a rule called deemed disposal where you are taxed every eight years on what your fund has gained, whether you sell it or not. The Government's own review of the funds sector recommended scrapping that rule back in 2024, but it is still there.

stories.title: Ukraine slams Russian drone 'safari' against civilians
stories.summary: Ukraine has expressed outrage over a video showing a man chased by a drone in Kherson city and denounced it as a deliberate "hunt" and "safari" targeting civilians. In the footage, which could not immediately be verified by AFP, a man seeks shelter behind a vehicle from a remotely piloted FPV (first-person view) drone pursuing him before detonating its explosive charge. The man, who was selling vegetables at a street market in the southern city, "suffered bodily injuries but survived", the head of Kherson City Military Administration, Yaroslav Shanko, said on Telegram. "I had only set up the umbrellas and began taking the crates out... My wife was there too. We heard a buzzing sound," the victim, a 52-year-old man identified as Yuriy, recounted in a video posted by local authorities.

stories.title: Bradley disappointed Rovers didn't score more goals
stories.summary: Shamrock Rovers manager Stephen Bradley admitted to feeling frustrated despite his side's 3-1 victory over Albanian outfit Egnatia in the Europa League third qualifying round. A 29th-minute penalty by Graham Burke, converted after Dylan Watts had been brought down, handed the League of Ireland side the lead at Tallaght Stadium before the visitors levelled, Guillem Jaime scoring on the rebound after goalkeeper Ed McGinty had saved his penalty. Pico Lopes fired the Hoops back in front from Jack Byrne’s pass in the 56th minute before Aaron Greene netted two minutes later to put them in control ahead of the return leg in Albania. However, Rovers could and should have added to their lead as Burke, Jonathan Afolabi and Jake Mulraney all had big chances to cap off an impressive second-half display with further goals.

stories.title: Moran: Mayo people's quirks helped form playing style
stories.summary: All-Ireland winning manager Andy Moran has conceded that his adventurous style of play was perhaps only successful due to the unique disposition of the Mayo people. Moran’s achievement was made all the greater due to it being his first year in charge, but ventures in other counties have opened his eyes to the necessity for a set of principles to be embraced by all. "I think that’s Mayo people," was Moran’s response when asked about his positivity being reflected in how his players executed the game-plan last weekend. "It’s knowing your own. Like you’ve seen over the last five, six, seven days, we’re an expressive county.

stories.title: Transfers: Ajax sign Ter Stegen ahead of Shels clash
stories.summary: Ajax have signed Barcelona goalkeeper Marc-Andre ter Stegen on loan ahead of their UEFA Conference League clash with Shelbourne on Wednesday. The German goalkeeper, the foreign player with the second-most appearances for the Spanish giants behind Lionel Messi, will move to the Amsterdam club until 30 July, 2027. It has been reported by Dutch media that Ter Stegen, as well as recent signings Julian Brandt and Tolu Arokodare, are set to be available for selection against the League of Ireland side at the Johan Cruyff Arena. He spent the second half of last season on loan at Girona FC.

stories.title: 10 must-see shows at Dublin Fringe Festival 2026
stories.summary: In her 2nd year as Dublin Fringe Festival Director, Bee Sparks highlights 10 must-see shows to consider for your festival diary this September. This is Dublin Fringe's boldest programme yet, a festival that takes over the city for 16 days and nights of exceptional, multidisciplinary work. This year the festival sets out to reignite our love affair with Dublin City, championing the irrepressible, indomitable creative force of Ireland’s artists and audiences, creating a festival that reflects the Ireland of today: the breadth of communities who call it home, the crucial conversations that shape our reality, and the visions that show us how things could be. Expect breath-taking performances across a sweeping spectrum of artforms - experience sharp new plays grappling with contemporary life - gas comedy to bring the belly-laughs - and interdisciplinary spectacle that forges new forms. The work at the festival will uncover hidden histories, bold futures and the beauty found right on your doorstep. Celebrate Ireland’s drag culture, bop to the best new hip-hop and R&B, and dance into the morning light. The best of international makes its home in Dublin this year too - from raucous gig theatre, quirky cabaret and breath-catching Zambian circus, to stepping behind the stage curtain to share your legacy with a tree. Now dive in! 1/ PHILOSOPHY OF THE WORLD from UK based live performance company, In Bed With My Brother. This is bold international work at it best and is presented in partnership with Project Arts Centre. In Bed With My Brother, have collaborations spanning theatre, performance, art, cabaret, music and nightlife, blending chaos, tongue-in-cheek humour and high-octane theatrical spectacle. Philosophy Of The World is a three-act biopic that attempts to wrangle the story of the best worst band of all time into an exciting new show for Dublin Fringe 2026. Part tribute act, part feminist reclamation, part rambling flight of ideas, this is about fate, freewill, power, patriarchy, band t-shirts, daddy issues and the best worst album ever made.

stories.title: Glen Hansard: A powerhouse of self-belief and passion
stories.summary: Back in Dublin's scuzzy early nineties music scene, nobody was quite sure what to make of Glen Hansard. The intense and passionate young fella from Ballymun with the long mane of red hair and the massive voice had first come to attention playing guitarist Outspan Foster in Alan Parker’s glorious adaption of Roddy Doyle’s novel The Commitments, a hilarious tale of the rise and fall of a young Dublin soul band. But it turned out this Hansard lad had a band of his own. They were called The Frames, named after the tangle of broken bicycles that could often be seen lying around his mother’s garden as he set about repairing them, and they were terribly unfashionable. At a time when ironic cool had supplanted rock 'n' roll passion, The Frames looked and sounded singularly out of step with what was going on around them. As for Glen, well, he was just too arty, too gauche. This windswept bohemian looked like he had just arrived fresh from Dublin’s 1960s folk boom.

stories.title: Is a side hustle the key to managing summer debt?
stories.summary: Holidays, summer camps, days out with friends and family and as many BBQs as the weather will allow... Summer can be an expensive time for all of us, and by the end of the season your wallet can be feeling the pinch. However, as Managing Director of Rockwell Financial, Robert Whelan, says, a summer side hustle can take the sting out of the high costs. He joined the Brendan O'Connor show to share his tips for managing debt this summer. First he suggests "triaging" our debts, especially with credit cards. Rather than staying a cycle of clearing just the minimum payments, Whelan says that clearing the debt entirely before addressing any others can be worthwhile as credit cards are the most expensive debts. "The principle behind triaging is being aware of it yourself", he says. "If you write down the amount and the interest rate beside it, it'll be very clear as to which one you should be clearing."

stories.title: Nearly 6,000 contact HSE for help finding a GP this year
stories.summary: Almost 6,000 people have contacted the Health Service Executive already this year seeking help in finding a GP. New figures also indicate that while Ireland's population increased by around 10% between 2020 and 2025, the total number of GPs increased by just 6.4%, as population growth continues to outstrip growth in services, creating a deficit of doctors to meet patient needs. The number of GPs treating patients with medical cards has risen by just 2.3% between 2020 and 2025, although the number of GPs entering private practice has increased by 26.8%. Just 59 GPs have signed up to provide care under the General Medical Services (GMS) scheme for patients with medical cards and GP visit cards since 2020.

stories.title: Stage-four cancer survivor hails rehabilitation trial
stories.summary: A man who is in remission from stage-four prostate cancer has said he is "a different person" after taking part in a 12-week rehabilitation trial. The pioneering cancer rehabilitation trial in Cork has received renewed funding from the Irish Cancer Society, with researchers hoping it will help make supportive rehabilitation a routine part of cancer care in Ireland. Launched in 2022, the LIAM Mc Trial (Linking In with Advice and supports for Men with Metastatic Cancer) saw men living with advanced prostate, bladder and kidney cancers receive specialist physiotherapy, nursing, dietetic advice and psychological support twice weekly over 12 weeks. Developed by Cancer Research at UCC and supported by €300,000 in funding from the Irish Cancer Society, the programme saw 56 men take part, with researchers noting an "overwhelmingly positive response" from participants.

stories.summary: Shamrock Rovers beat KF Egnatia of Albania by 3-1 in the first leg of their UEFA Europa League third qualifying round tie at Tallaght Stadium, but it could have been so much more had the home side taken their chances in a dominant second-half display. Rovers had to be content with the win that was engineered by a Graham Burke penalty, a Pico Lopes header, and a goal by Aaron Greene from Jack Byrne's corner which gave Rovers a two-goal advantage to take to next weeks second leg in Rrogozhinë. Under leaden skies and the distant roll of thunder, the pitch glistened as persistent rainfall soaked the ground, delivering some much-needed moisture before the game. The home side started ex-Irish Internationals Burke, Byrne, and Enda Stevens with Will Fitzgerald, who make his debut for the club against Drogheda last Friday, also in the starting XI.

stories.title: Ospreys or Scarlets face axe as WRU outlines cut plans
stories.summary: Wales are to go ahead with plans to cut their number of professional franchises from four to three, spelling the end for either the Ospreys or Scarlets, both former winners of the United Rugby Championship. The Welsh Rugby Union on Wednesday confirmed the proposed change to the professional game and plans to establish three men's teams from the 2028/29 season – one based in the capital, one in west Wales and one in east Wales. Cardiff, owned by the Welsh Rugby Union, and Dragons, an independently backed business, are set to be given licences, leaving Swansea-based Ospreys and Llanelli-based Scarlets to compete for the remaining spot. Ospreys have won the URC, in its previous guise, four times, most recently in 2012.

stories.title: In the arena - John Healy's long road back from literary oblivion
stories.summary: Ahead of a special IFI screening of his acclaimed documentary Barbaric Genius, filmmaker Paul Duane reflects on the life and literary legacy of the film's subject, Grass Arena author John Healy. The first time I spoke to John Healy, over the phone in 2007, I remember feeling not quite frightened, but possibly intimidated, approaching him. This was a man with a legend around him, a man who had emerged from the underclass with an incendiary memoir telling stories not only of violence and squalor but also of great intellectual abilities that were rendered invisible by Healy's position as Irish and working-class in fifties Britain. A memoir that came dressed in the black and green hardback livery of Faber & Faber, but which emerged from the recognisable world of London's squares and squats, a London I recognised from my time spent there, seeing for the first time how the left-behind of the Irish diaspora existed in a state of desperation made bearable by whatever drugs and alcohol they could scrounge.

stories.title: What should a perimenopausal skincare routine look like?
stories.summary: If the moisturiser you have sworn by for years suddenly doesn’t feel rich enough, or spots are appearing at the same time as dry, sensitive patches, perimenopause could be playing a part. There’s plenty of advice about "menopausal skin", usually centred around dryness, thinning and loss of collagen. But perimenopause – the transitional years leading up to menopause – can be slightly more complicated. Rather than oestrogen remaining consistently low, hormone levels fluctuate during perimenopause. This can make skin feel somewhat unpredictable: oily or spot-prone one month, dry and sensitive the next, with changes in texture, pigmentation and firmness potentially appearing, too. According to dermatological doctor Dr Nora Jaafar, her clients often think "skin suddenly becomes ‘older’ overnight. In reality, it’s responding to changing hormones".

stories.title: Armed man arrested at Trump's California golf course
stories.summary: An armed man has been arrested at US President Donald Trump's golf course in Los Angeles two days before the US leader's visit, the local sheriff's office said. The suspect, identified as 38-year-old Jeanine John Taele from nearby Downey, California, was arrested on Sunday afternoon at the golf course in Rancho Palos Verdes. Plainclothes federal agents spotted him "walking throughout the golf course grounds taking photographs and videos and appearing to monitor security-planning activities," the sheriff's office said in a statement. Mr Trump arrived by helicopter at the golf club yesterday evening to attend a fundraising dinner hosted by the Republican National Committee.

stories.summary: Fórsa union members at Oberstown Children Detention Campus have carried out a six-hour work stoppage. stories.title: Labour's Bev Craig elected mayor of Greater Manchester
stories.summary: The UK's ruling Labour Party comfortably retained the mayoralty of Greater Manchester following an election triggered by new Prime Minister Andy Burnham's return to parliament. Bev Craig, the leader of Manchester City Council, was elected after winning 47.15% of the votes in the first round. The anti-immigration Reform UK party, which had been riding high in national polls, came in second place with a 21% share. Without the 50% of votes needed to win outright, the counting proceeded to a second round.

stories.title: Next ups profit outlook again on warm weather sales boost
stories.summary: UK clothing retailer Next has today edged up its annual profit outlook for the third time this year, as it reported a better-than-expected 9.2% rise in second-quarter full-price sales, benefiting from the warm weather. Shares in Next, which trades from more than 800 stores in the UK and Ireland and has an online operation serving the UK and overseas, rose 7% in early trade, extending their gain so far in 2026 to 19%. Next had forecast that second-quarter full-price sales growth would slow to 4% after growth of 6.2% in its first quarter, reflecting a tough comparative number in the same period last year. However, sales were £70m ahead of forecast in the 13 weeks to August 1 - £19m in the UK and £51m overseas.

stories.title: Ukrainian strikes on holiday resort, Crimea kill 11
stories.summary: Ukrainian strikes, one in a Russian Black Sea resort and another in the annexed peninsula of Crimea, have killed a total of 11 people and wounded dozens, officials have said. Russia said seven people, including three children, had been killed and about 40 injured at the holiday resort of Gelendzhik, in what it said was a deliberate Ukrainian drone attack on civilians. Social media videos, verified by Reuters, showed what appears to be a drone slamming into a busy beach area near the town of Gelendzhik, accompanied by a loud explosion. Reuters confirmed the location from the buildings, coastline and trees matched satellite and archive imagery.
